The plan is approved. I’ll rename the minutes to the meeting dates, add the index, and check that the note text itself did not change.The renames are in place. The editor is still blocked by plan mode, so I’ll add the index from the shell.The index is written. Next I’ll check checksums, headings, and that every index link points at a real file.Two index lines say work was finished when the minutes only assign it. I’ll correct those before I stop.The minutes in `notes/` now use `YYYY-MM-DD.md`, and `notes/README.md` lists all seven meetings from oldest to newest.

| Old name | New name |
| --- | --- |
| `aug11.md` | `2026-08-11.md` |
| `minutes 25 aug.md` | `2026-08-26.md` |
| `Meeting sept 8.md` | `2026-09-08.md` |
| `notes_2026-09-22.md` | `2026-09-22.md` |
| `oct6 meeting notes.md` | `2026-10-06.md` |
| `2026.10.20 minutes.md` | `2026-10-20.md` |
| `Nov 3 (final).md` | `2026-11-03.md` |

`2026-08-26.md` follows the heading. The meeting was held on 26 August after the 25 August date was cancelled because of the storm. The index says that.

What I checked:

- Each minute’s SHA-1 matches the checksum taken before the rename, so the note text is unchanged.
- Each heading date matches its filename.
- The seven old names are gone.
- The index has seven links, in date order, and each one opens a file in `notes/`.
- The root `README.md` and `members.csv` still have the same checksums as before.
- The index lines match the minutes. Two lines were tightened after that read: 11 August only agrees to move the shed lights to the night rate, and 22 September still has the compost order ahead of it.
